construction.note: The wheel follows Sandy Kurt’s 8fold Zellige PDF. Its circles, octagons and central rosette are sourced; the final ink was read from her finished drawing.
construction.changes: We added an edge-to-edge square repeat. The PDF teaches one wheel. The app splits, combines and reorders its operations, so its step numbers are not the PDF’s. The repeat is not presented as a historical reconstruction.

credits.creator: Sandy Kurt
credits.note: The construction follows her nineteen steps, and the lines inked are those of her finished drawing; the step text is our own.

given.A: Any point to the right of O. The distance OA is the radius of the main circle, and the unit for every length.

steps.text: Draw a circle with centre O through A. Its radius is the unit for the whole pattern.
Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at E, N, W and S. These letters stand for east, north, west and south.
Draw the lines through O that halve the angles at O between E and N, and between N and W. These lines cross the circle at NE, NW, SW and SE.
Join E, N, W and S with straight lines. Join NE, NW, SW and SE with straight lines. The two squares cross at X1 to X8.
Draw a straight line through O and each of X1, X2, X3 and X4. The circle is now cut into sixteen.
Draw a circle with centre X1 that just touches the horizontal line and the line through O and NE. Draw circles of the same size with centres X2 to X8 and O. These are the ring circles.

Draw a straight line through X1 and X4, X5 and X8, X2 and X7, and X3 and X6. Draw a straight line through X1 and X6, X2 and X5, X3 and X8, and X4 and X7. Each line joins the centres of two ring circles.
Draw a circle with centre M that just touches the vertical line and the line through O and NE. M is where the line through X1 and X4 crosses the line through O and X2.
Draw a circle with centre O that just touches this small circle on its near side. Draw circles of the same size with centres X1 to X8.

Draw a circle with centre R1 that just touches the ring circle at X1 on its near side. R1 is where the line through X1 and X6 crosses the line through X3 and X8. Draw circles of the same size with centres R2 to R8, where the other joining lines cross.
Draw a straight line through X1 and X3, X2 and X4, X3 and X5, and X4 and X6. Draw a straight line through X5 and X7, X6 and X8, X7 and X1, and X8 and X2. The eight lines make two more squares.
Draw vertical lines in pairs. They go through the points where the circles round X1 to X8 cross the lines of step 11.
Draw horizontal lines in pairs. They go through the points where the circles round X1 to X8 cross the lines of step 11.
Draw lines that slope up to the left in pairs. They go through the points where the circles round X1 to X8 cross the lines of step 11.
Draw lines that slope up to the right in pairs. They go through the points where the circles round X1 to X8 cross the lines of step 11.
Draw an octagon in each ring circle, each small circle and the circle round O. Its corners are where the circle crosses the lines through its centre that run parallel to the lines through O.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw an octagon in each ring circle, each small circle and the circle round O. Its corners are where the circle crosses the lines through its centre that run parallel to the lines through O.

steps.text: Mark Z1 to Z16, where the circle round O crosses the sixteen lines through O. Join each mark to the marks three places round, with straight lines in pairs. This makes the star in the middle.
Draw a vertical line through each of E and W. Draw a horizontal line through each of N and S. Join T1, T2, T3 and T4, where they cross, to mark the square tile that repeats.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Join T1, T2, T3 and T4 to mark the square tile that repeats. Its corners are crossings already on the board.

ink.text: Ink the lines of the finished wheel: the octagons, the bands between them and the star in the middle. Follow the faint grey ink, or tick “Also ink the copies round the centre” to ink eight at once.

pattern.text: Put copies of the tile side by side. Neighbouring wheels touch at the corners of their large octagons.

expect.note: Golden values in units of OA (the main circle's radius), computed by the engine. The kites and the thin star between wheels are small by design.
